samples.marker_line: Posh-SecMod: upstream audit tool; add IIS credential-query traits
execution_trace: The fetched darkoperator/Posh-SecMod master/PostExploitation/PostExploitation.psm1 is byte-identical: SHA-256 21e577ac4e1199aff6c4dd53b78ee15b6361dc9ce4e1b22db4b44f8db255797a.
Top-level code defines 12 functions. There is no module-load payload invocation, fixed callback host, persistence, or automatic exfiltration.
ConvertTo-PostBase64Command encodes caller text or a selected file as UTF-16LE Base64. Compress-PostScript creates Deflate+Base64 data and returns a decompression/Invoke-Expression command.

New-PostDownloadExecuteScript returns an encoded downloader/evaluator with an explicitly supplied URL and system proxy credentials. New-PostDownloadExecutePE returns a downloader that converts space-delimited byte values, writes a randomized EXE, and requests hidden execution. Despite the Hex function names, those PE conversion routines serialize decimal byte values rather than hexadecimal text.
Start-PostRemoteProcess explicitly queries Win32_Process at the supplied ComputerName with supplied credentials and invokes Create on the returned WMI class with caller command text.

Get-PostHashdumpScript returns source or a compressed command. Its payload enables SeDebugPrivilege, opens and duplicates the LSASS token, assigns it to the thread, reads LSA class strings for the boot key and SAM F/V records, then uses MD5/RC4 and RID-derived DES keys to output username:RID:LM:NT hashes. This is registry hash extraction, not an LSASS memory dump.

Get-PostReverTCPShell returns source or encoded text. The payload connects TcpClient to caller LHOST/LPORT, starts COMSPEC with redirected stdin/stdout, reads commands from the socket into shell stdin, and returns shell output over the stream.

Get-PostCopyNTDS returns source or a compressed command. It checks KDC/admin/SYSTEM context, impersonates SYSTEM if needed, starts VSS, creates a snapshot, reflectively invokes Win32Native.CopyFile on the snapshot NTDS.dit into TEMP, and deletes its snapshot/restores VSS status. The missing space in Get-WMIObjectwin32_shadowcopy prevents assuming runtime success. Cleanup of its own snapshot is not recovery-inhibition evidence.

Get-Webconfig explicitly enumerates IIS virtual directories with AppCmd, reads web.config XML, extracts database usernames/passwords, and constructs aspnet_regiis -pdf connectionStrings to decrypt protected sections in a temporary copy.

Get-ApplicationHost constructs and evaluates AppCmd queries for application-pool and virtual-directory usernames/passwords, returning local tabular results. No network send is present in these recovery functions.
The only decoded Base64 payload is the documentation example write-host hello world (with quotes around hello world); no concealed malicious stage was recovered.

All seven URLs in the module occur in comments/help, not download configuration. Referenced code is already embedded and Windows/.NET/IIS components are platform dependencies; no third-party runtime fetch or import dependency is configured.
samples.reason_for_external_malware_label: The supplied AV labels include PUP/PUA/riskware and PowerDump/SEToolkit names. Shared offensive routines explain these detections without a trojanized module. Benign classification is supported by exact upstream provenance, transparent operator-driven design and absence of added automation; actual usage/authorization on a particular machine is unknown.

changes.scope: Parsed PowerShell assignments on Windows; descriptions assert command construction rather than import-time execution. Full-node queries avoid the engine kind-cache 100-character evidence truncation.

remaining_disagreements: Engine-emitted binary/embedded/base64-powershell remains suspicious on the harmless hello-world documentation example. This is not a YAML trait and no YAML shadow or broad suppressor was introduced.

Third-party Empire Invoke-Powerdump and Powerup labels match shared PowerDump and NetSPI source. They are pattern matches, not proof that this artifact is Empire. Their notable detections remain retained; bundled upstream YARA attribution metadata is outside this YAML change.

No calibrated classifier-verdict disagreement: all model cls values remain 0, level -1 (BENIGN), although the Posh-SecMod raw probability remains high. Atomscan reports model v18 feature compatibility with a v19 extractor; scores were not used to establish behavior.
